first_impression: The title screen sold me straight away: a golden sunset over low-poly pines, a chunky woolly serif logo and cosy felt menus. Then the first evening was over in about 30 seconds with three stars and four minutes of daylight left, and the wolves the HUD keeps counting down to never actually showed up until the last minute of the video.
best_things: The menus and briefing cards are lovely (00:00, 00:48, 02:42, 07:18): each evening gets a painted backdrop, a title like 'Old Angus' or 'Mist on the Moor' and a 'New tonight' rule, so every level feels like an episode.

The herding itself reads at a glance: the dashed ring round Pip, the flock bunching and fleeing as one blob, and hearts and gold rings popping as sheep pour into the fold (00:24, 02:12, 05:51) make the goal and the result obvious.

There is a real season to work through: a grid of nine evenings with stars, ribbons and charms (00:03), and each one changes something (lambs, a stubborn ram, mist, a storm that floods the ford, snow, a night watch), with the snowy bridge evening (07:21-08:48) and the moonlit watch (08:51) looking the best.

worst_problems.problem: The sunset and wolves, the whole source of tension, basically never happen. Evening 1 ends with 4:00 of daylight left and no wolf in sight, every montage clip finishes or cuts with the 'wolves come out in' timer still running (02:39, 04:09, 07:15, 08:48), and the only wolves in ten minutes are two tiny red-ringed silhouettes at the very edge of the screen in the night watch (09:06, 09:30) that nothing ever happens with.
worst_problems.suggestion: Tune the evenings so a normal player is still herding when the sun goes down, or bring a wolf in early in the first two evenings, and make a wolf encounter a big readable on-screen moment instead of an edge icon.

worst_problems.problem: A lot of the footage is Pip jogging alone across an empty lawn or slowly nudging one small flock over the same featureless grass. The game even admits it with a 'Long way to the next sheep? Hold Shift to sprint' tip.
worst_problems.suggestion: Shrink the gaps between flocks or give the travel something to do: obstacles, gates, a straggler on the way, a stray lamb, or a faster 'outrun' move that sends Pip round a flock automatically.

worst_problems.problem: In First Snow the flock jams at the east end of the bridge for almost a full minute while Pip and the dark ram stand at the west end; from frame to frame nothing changes. It looks like a stalemate or a pathing bug, not a puzzle.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make bridges funnel the flock more forgivingly, and if the ram is blocking, show it clearly (a prompt or icon over him) so the player knows what to do instead of circling.

worst_problems.problem: Mist on the Moor is a flat beige-white screen with a small bubble of ground round Pip. White sheep are white puffs against white fog, and for long stretches Pip runs through blank nothing.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make the fog a darker, cooler grey with some depth so silhouettes of rocks, trees and sheep ghost through it, and show bleats as visible ripples or arrows at the edge of the bubble.

worst_problems.problem: Unexplained things on the ground: a bright glowing yellow orb keeps popping up in random spots in daylight and at night, and the storm evening is littered with black specks round the flock. I could not tell if they are collectibles, birds, fireflies, mud or a lens flare.
worst_problems.suggestion: Either make them clearly something (a firefly with a trail, crows that flap and lift off) or tone them down so they do not look like pickups or glitches.

boredom_points: 01:15-02:03: nearly a minute of slowly pushing one small flock down the side of the stream on the same mustard-coloured grass.
03:09-03:21 and 03:45-03:51: Pip running solo across the valley to find the next group of sheep.
05:03-05:27: Pip running through blank fog with nothing on screen but himself and a path.
07:57-08:48: the flock stuck at the snowy bridge while nothing changes.
08:51-09:15: the night watch opens with Pip standing beside a sleeping flock; it looks like four minutes of waiting with the occasional wolf at the edge of the screen.
confusions: Lambing Time (00:51-02:39) says to keep each lamb with its mother, but from this camera I could not tell a single lamb from a ewe.
What is the glowing yellow orb that appears all over the map (01:27, 03:36, 04:33, 09:03)?
What are the black specks scattered around the sheep in the storm (05:45, 06:03, 06:51)?
The HUD counts down to the wolves every evening, but the evenings end or cut before they come, so I never learned what a wolf attack looks like or how to stop one.
The small orange round markers at the screen edge (00:27, 01:15, 04:15) are too small to read: fold, lamb or sheep?
At 07:57-08:48 I could not tell why the flock would not cross the bridge or what the dark sheep next to Pip was doing.
Three stars after 30 seconds on evening 1 (00:42) made me unsure what the stars are actually rewarding.
wish_list: Let me see the sunset turn and the wolves come out in the first couple of evenings, so the pitch's tension is there from the start.
A lower or zoomable camera now and then, so the hills, sky and sunset from the menu art show up during play instead of only a lawn from above.
More landmarks and texture on the ground: sheep tracks, hedges, gates to open, gullies, so driving a flock means choosing a route.
Visible sound cues in the mist (bleat ripples), and a clearer look for lambs and the black sheep.
A pat-the-dog moment or a little celebration animation for Pip when the gate closes.
Time or score challenges per evening (a ghost of my best run, or a daily seed) to give a reason to replay three-starred evenings.
one_line_review: A gorgeous, cosy herding game with a real season of evenings to work through, but in this footage the sunset and wolves barely show up, so most evenings are a calm jog across a mustard lawn.
